memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Migraine and dyslipidaemia.
Patient reports episodic throbbing headaches twice weekly, associated nausea, photophobia; no focal neurology. Lipid panel not yet done. She is a non‑smoker (never smoked, pack‑years 0). Examination: vitals normal, no meningism, cranial nerves II‑XII intact, cardiopulmonary normal. Neurological examination shows no abnormal signs. Plan: start propranolol 40 mg OD for migraine prevention, sumatriptan 50 mg SOS for acute attacks, atorvastatin 10 mg HS for dyslipidaemia, advise low‑saturated‑fat diet and aerobic exercise. Review in 3 months.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Migraine and dyslipidaemia.
Headache frequency reduced to once weekly, mild intensity, sumatriptan used twice in month. Lipids show LDL still elevated, triglycerides borderline. Non‑smoker. Exam: vitals stable, no neurological deficit. Plan: continue propranolol, add topiramate 25 mg HS for migraine prophylaxis, increase atorvastatin to 20 mg HS, recheck labs in 2 months.

memories.text: I’ve been getting headaches about three times a month now, usually moderate, and I take sumatriptan when needed. I feel a bit tired after starting topiramate.

memories.text:
Migraine and dyslipidaemia.
Headache frequency now twice weekly, mild‑moderate, topiramate causing mild paresthesia. Lipids: LDL 122, HDL 50, TG 158. Non‑smoker. Exam: normal. Plan: keep propranolol, reduce topiramate to 25 mg OD (split), continue atorvastatin 20 mg HS, add fenofibrate 145 mg OD for triglycerides, recheck labs in 3 months.
